## B — Audience, level and prerequisites: getting your Nevada license (eligibility, documents, residency and testing)
Audience: first-time Nevada Basic Class C applicants, new residents transferring an out-of-state license, and applicants weighing a Driver Authorization Card.
Why it matters to a first-timer: the application rules, minimum age and required proofs come first [A01], and the Testing page tells the applicant what the knowledge and road tests check [A07].
Level: procedural recall with several exact thresholds (minimum age, days to transfer, validity years, waiver look-back periods, fees); low conceptual load.
Prerequisites: none; this is the opening chapter of the handbook.

corpus_stability.reason: The Nevada Driver's Handbook carries one edition line on its cover (DMV 700 March 2024) and one copyright year on its title page, with a short key-changes list; nothing in the selected pages suggests more than one rewrite per year. The edition is about two and a half years old at intake, so currency is held as freshness debt in part A.
